title: Free colimit with residue-injective transitions over a henselian local base
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings (the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $B$ is the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$), essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Suppose $A$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $P$ be a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] which is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. There exist a small filtered category $D$ and a diagram of free $A$-modules $F_d$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with $A$-linear transition maps $t_a:F_d\to F_e$ for arrows $a:d\to e$, and compatible $A$-linear maps $v_d:F_d\to P$, such that $(P,(v_d))$ is a colimit of this diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and every induced map $F_d/\mathfrak mF_d\to F_e/\mathfrak mF_e$ is injective. The free modules need not have finite rank; $\mathfrak mF_d$ denotes the submodule generated by the products $ax$ for $a\in\mathfrak m$ and $x\in F_d$.

source.place: Tag 05U7 (lemma-flat-finite-type-local-colimit-free), first assertion, omitting the additional Mittag-Leffler conclusion.

proof.text: Choose a finite-type $A$-algebra $C$ and a multiplicative set $W$ with $B=W^{-1}C$. Put $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_B\cap C$. Every element of $C\setminus\mathfrak q$ maps to a unit of $B$, so the mutually inverse localization maps identify $C_{\mathfrak q}=B$. Choose generators $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ of $P$ over $B$, and let $K$ be the kernel of $C^r\to P$, $(c_i)\mapsto\sum c_ip_i$. Set $M=C^r/K$. Then $M_{\mathfrak q}\to P$ is an isomorphism: coefficients in $B=C_{\mathfrak q}$ give surjectivity; if a vector divided by $s\notin\mathfrak q$ maps to zero, its numerator already maps to zero and belongs to $K$. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $x=\mathfrak q$, and $\mathcal F=\widetilde M$. The principal-open sections theorem makes $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent, and its affine finite-type criterion makes it of finite type. Taking germs of the principal-open localization formula gives $\mathcal F_x=M_{\mathfrak q}=P$ as $A$-modules. Locality of $A\to B$ gives $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m$, so $x$ is in the closed fibre.

Put $k=A/\mathfrak m$, $R=C/\mathfrak mC$, and $H=M/\mathfrak mM$. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$); $R$ is finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian by the finite-type algebra theorem. The images of the chosen $r$ generators generate $H$ over $R$. The affine pullback formula identifies the closed-fibre module $\mathcal F_s$ on $X_s=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $\widetilde H$. By finiteness of associated primes and the affine associated-point dictionary, $T=\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(\mathcal F_s)$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 05U7, shrinking the closed fibre; Tags 00LC and 02OK for finiteness

proof.text: For each $y\in T$ which does not specialize to $x$, write its prime as $\mathfrak p_y\subset R$ and choose $\bar h_y\in\mathfrak p_y\setminus\bar{\mathfrak q}$, where $\bar{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q/\mathfrak mC$. Such an element exists because specialization to $x$ means $\mathfrak p_y\subseteq\bar{\mathfrak q}$. Lift $\prod_y\bar h_y$ to $h\in C$ (the empty product is $1$). Then $x\in D(h)$ and no bad $y$ lies in $D(h)_s$. Replace $X$ by $D(h)$ and $\mathcal F$ by its restriction. Associated points are defined by their local module stalks; restriction to an open leaves those stalks unchanged, so the associated points of the new closed fibre are exactly $T\cap D(h)_s$. Every such point now specializes to $x$. The stalk at $x$ remains $P$.

source.place: Tag 05U7, sentence beginning After shrinking X

proof.text: For every open neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ in this $X$, apply the free-affine-neighbourhood theorem to $W\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\mathcal F|_W$. Its hypotheses hold: local finite type and finite-type quasi-coherence persist on open restriction; $x$ lies over $\mathfrak m$; its stalk is the given $A$-flat module $P$; and $A$ is henselian. Thus some affine $U$ with $x\in U\subseteq W$ has $F_U=\Gamma(U,\mathcal F)$ free over $A$. Let $D$ consist of all such affine opens, with a unique arrow $U\to V$ when $V\subseteq U$. It is small, being a subset of the set of opens of $X$. It is nonempty, and for any two objects apply the same theorem inside $U\cap V$ to obtain a common target. Parallel arrows are equal. Therefore $D$ is filtered. Restriction gives its transition maps and germs give compatible maps $v_U:F_U\to P$.

source.place: Tag 05U7, fundamental system of free affine neighbourhoods

proof.text: For $U\to V$ in $D$, put $U_s=U\times_A k$ and $V_s=V\times_A k$, the inverse images of $U$ and $V$ in the closed fibre $X_s$; they are open in $X_s$, and by the affine fibre-product theorem $U_s\cong\operatorname{Spec}(\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)\otimes_Ak)$ and likewise for $V_s$, so they are affine opens of the closed fibre. Affine base change gives $k\otimes_A F_U\cong\Gamma(U_s,\mathcal F_s)$ and the corresponding isomorphism for $V$. The quotient identification $k\otimes_A F\cong F/\mathfrak mF$ sends $\bar a\otimes z$ to $az\bmod\mathfrak mF$, with inverse $z\bmod\mathfrak mF\mapsto1\otimes z$. The base-change formula on pure tensors sends $\bar a\otimes z$ to $\bar a\eta(z)$. Since restrictions of the pullback unit commute with restriction of $z$, these identifications carry the reduction of $F_U\to F_V$ to the actual restriction $\Gamma(U_s,\mathcal F_s)\to\Gamma(V_s,\mathcal F_s)$.

source.place: Tag 05U7, displayed closed-fibre restriction map; affine base change Tag 01I9

proof.text: Let $z\in\Gamma(U_s,\mathcal F_s)$ restrict to zero on $V_s$. The principal opens of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ contained in $U_s$ cover $U_s$. Each has coordinate ring $R_f$, Noetherian by localization permanence, so $U_s$ is locally Noetherian by its affine-cover definition. Its section module is finite over its coordinate ring by the affine finite-type criterion. If $z\ne0$, the associated-stalk detection theorem applied to $z$ and $0$ supplies $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_{U_s}(\mathcal F_s|_{U_s})$ with $z_y\ne0$. Associatedness depends only on the stalk, so $y$ is associated on $X_s$ as well. Step 3 says $y$ specializes to $x$; the open $V_s$ contains $x$, hence contains its generalization $y$. But $z|_{V_s}=0$ gives $z_y=0$, a contradiction. Thus every reduction of a transition map is injective.

source.place: Tag 05U7, kernel supported away from x; associated-point detection as in Tag 0B3M

proof.text: The germs identify the colimit with $P$ directly. Every element of $P=\mathcal F_x$ has a section representative on a neighbourhood of $x$; step 4 supplies an object of $D$ inside it. If two sections on objects of $D$ have the same germ, the stalk equality criterion gives an open neighbourhood on which they agree, and step 4 supplies an object of $D$ inside its intersection with their domains. For an arbitrary $A$-module $Q$ and a compatible family $a_U:F_U\to Q$, send a germ represented by $z\in F_U$ to $a_U(z)$. The preceding equality criterion proves this well-defined. A common refinement shows it respects sums and $A$-scalars. It factors every $a_U$ and is unique because every germ has such a representative. This is the module-colimit universal property, completing the assertion.
